method: PARAPHRASED AND HASH-ANCHORED from The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema' (last updated January 2024). Every claim is a paraphrase backed by anchors (scripts/anchor.py): verify.py --source re-finds each anchored span in a fresh copy of the source, checks the claim's numbers against it and rejects copying. LICENCE: © The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne; Terms clause 5.2, personal use only; paraphrased and hash-anchored (read at RCH Terms and Conditions, clause 5.2 (rch.org.au)). The source's words are NOT reproduced here. Edition 2.0 rebuilds the Wave 1 hand-written edition (verbatim quotes) as paraphrase against the page fetched 2026-09-24. Every clinical claim of edition 1.0 is carried over; the last-updated claim now sits in the source date. The fingertip-unit table is a grid rendered as text: its values are anchored as one block, so confirm the alignment on the live page. No antibiotic or antiviral agent or dose appears in the source and none is supplied.

claims.claim: **Eczema affects 30% of children** and often starts before 12 months of age; for some it lasts for life.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Children with eczema need good daily skin care whatever their skin looks like.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Topical steroids, used properly, are both safe and effective — and flares cannot be treated without them.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Do not ration steroids or build in regular breaks during a flare.** Apply them generously, then moisturiser on top.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Used according to guidelines, topical steroids do not cause** skin atrophy, hypopigmentation, hypertrichosis, osteoporosis, purpura or telangiectasia. Striae, adrenal suppression and eye disease are rare and reported only after long, excessive use of potent agents.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Broken or infected skin can still have steroid applied.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Give every child with eczema a home management plan** that includes what to do in a flare.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Work out how much steroid cream to apply with the Fingertip Unit method.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Fingertip units by area, for ages 3-12 months / over 1-3 / over 3-6 / over 6-10 / over 10 years:** face & neck 1 / 1½ / 1½ / 2 / 2½ · arm & hand 1 / 1½ / 2 / 2½ / 4 · leg & foot 1½ / 2 / 3 / 4½ / 8 · front of chest & abdomen 1 / 2 / 3 / 3½ / 8 · back & buttocks 1½ / 3 / 3½ / 5 / 7.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Apply topical steroid once or twice a day until the skin is fully clear,** to settle the inflammation.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Face or groin, mild to moderate flare:** a mild-potency steroid such as hydrocortisone 1% (ointment or cream).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Face or groin, severe flare:** a moderate-potency steroid such as methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% (ointment or cream), short courses only — no more than 3-5 days on face and neck, 7-14 days on the groin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Body:** mild to moderate flare → moderate potency, e.g. methylprednisolone aceponate 0.1% (as a cream, ointment or fatty ointment) · severe flare → potent, e.g. mometasone furoate 0.1% (ointment or cream).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Very potent steroids (such as betamethasone dipropionate 0.05%) only with dermatology advice.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **How often:** hydrocortisone twice daily, mometasone or methylprednisolone once daily — in each case until symptoms clear.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Form:** ointments beat creams because they moisturise better; use lotions on hairy skin such as the scalp.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Pimecrolimus 1% cream** is a second-line option for mild to moderate flares in sensitive areas, for children over 3 months. Keep each course to 6 weeks at most (3 weeks for ages 3-23 months).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Mild to moderate eczema on the face: use a low-potency steroid,** so the skin is not chemically irritated.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Moisturise the whole body generously twice daily, and after baths,** with a thick, plain cream that is high in oil and low in water.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Skip moisturisers with fragrance, alcohol, sodium lauryl sulfate, or plant or food ingredients** (milk from cows or goats; nut, olive or vegetable oils): they can damage the skin barrier and sensitise the skin.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Keep hand bacteria out of the tub:** scoop cream out with a spoon or spatula.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Bathe daily where the water supply allows,** to cut bacterial load on the skin and the chance of infection; keep water lukewarm (under 31°C).
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **No soap and no shampoo** — use a soap-free cleanser that will not irritate.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Bath oil (a capful) may go in the water, but it makes the child more likely to slip,** so an adult must always supervise directly.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Contact dermatitis culprits to avoid:** washes, cleansers or hair products containing MI (methylisothiazolinone) or MCI (methylchloroisothiazolinone), and any nappy wipe with benzalkonium chloride.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Layer moisturiser over steroid or other topical medicines,** not under.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Allergy tests are rarely needed and elimination diets rarely help;** parents should see a dermatologist or general paediatrician before cutting foods out.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Non-sedating antihistamines do nothing for eczema itch;** consider them only when urticaria or allergic rhinitis is also present.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Why treatment fails:** poor education about eczema and its treatments; not enough moisturiser, steroid or wet dressing applied; continued trigger exposure; skin infection missed or untreated; MRSA.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Flares usually trace back to** caregivers not being taught enough about management, and to triggers — infection, irritants, heat.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Wet dressings** put moisture back into the skin, shield it from infection and more damage, and ease irritation and itch. Use them with every flare, 1-4 times a day for at least 3 days; they can be used on infected eczema alongside antimicrobials.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **For facial itch, a cool compress** (a cloth or towel soaked in water, bath oil or both) gives instant relief.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Bleach baths can be used every day during a flare** to lower skin bacteria. Wet the face and head but do not put them under the water.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Where it appears:** in infants, mostly the cheeks, scalp and extensor surfaces; in older children, the flexures — elbow and knee creases, neck, front of the ankles, around the eyes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Severity:** clear — normal skin, no active eczema · mild — dry patches, itch now and then, perhaps small red areas · moderate — dry patches, frequent itch and redness, perhaps excoriation and local thickening · severe — widespread dryness, constant itch and redness, perhaps excoriation, extensive thickening, bleeding, oozing, cracking and pigment change.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Signs of infected eczema:** in the skin — rising itch; lesions that are crusted, vesicular, satellite, pustular, eroded, tender, scabbed or weeping; systemically — fever and malaise.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **What each infection looks like:** bacterial — itchy yellow crusts, weeping, pustules, folliculitis · ⚠️ herpeticum — painful grouped blisters and punched-out erosions · coxsackium — vesiculobullous rash with brownish colour and satellite lesions around the eczema.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **A new itchy rash in several family members: think of scabies.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Discoid eczema tends to persist and resist treatment,** often needing longer courses of potent steroids.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Tests are usually unnecessary.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Broken eczematous skin is at high risk of bacterial and viral infection.** Usual organisms: Staphylococcus aureus (think of MRSA if first-line antibiotics fail or the child is in a high-risk group) and Streptococcus pyogenes.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Soak crusts off gently with a cloth in the bath first;** steroid and moisturiser go on only once the crusts are gone.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Systemic features or severe infection may mean admission for intravenous antibiotics.**
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Viral infection often sits alongside bacterial infection;** suspect it when infected eczema is not improving on antibiotics.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Eczema herpeticum (herpes simplex): start antivirals promptly;** severe cases may need them intravenously. Around the eyes → urgent ophthalmology review.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Recurrent infection:** consider Staphylococcus aureus decolonisation (child and family); antiseptics such as bleach baths, triclosan cleanser or chlorhexidine wash may lower skin bacteria.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: ⚠️ **Consider the local paediatric team for:** eczema herpeticum or severe bacterial infection; moderate or severe eczema not improving after 2 weeks or more of correctly followed treatment; carers who cannot deliver treatment and cannot reach outpatient support; severe eczema under 12 months of age; poor feeding, poor sleep or failure to thrive; suspected systemic disease (immunodeficiency, micronutrient deficiency); suspected coexisting severe allergy.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Consider dermatology** for chronic eczema that stays uncontrolled despite optimised topical treatment and daily skin care, so systemic therapy can be considered.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24

claims.claim: **Prescribe generously:** several quantities and repeats of each medicine, with PBS authority where it applies.
claims.locator: The Royal Children's Hospital Melbourne, 'Clinical Practice Guideline: Eczema', last updated January 2024, https://www.rch.org.au/clinicalguide/guideline_index/Eczema/, retrieved 2026-09-24
